# Physical constants — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/physical-constants.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/physical-constants.ttl`](../decks/physical-constants.ttl) · **Cards:** 70 · **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

35 fundamental physical constants in 70 cards: the seven exact defining constants of the SI, constants derived exactly from them, and measured constants of electromagnetism, atomic physics and gravitation, including the Planck units. For each constant one card asks for its standard symbol and one for its value (with unit where it has one). Values are exact where the SI makes them exact; otherwise they are the CODATA 2022 recommended values rounded to 5 significant figures and marked ≈. Values use a decimal point, as in CODATA's tables, and digits grouped in threes; the Swedish notes follow Swedish practice with a decimal comma. Compiled from the CODATA 2022 report (arXiv), the BIPM SI Brochure, Swedac's regulations on units (STAFS 2009:26) and Wikidata, and checked against NIST's CODATA tables.

## Licensing

The deck is CC BY 4.0. Its content sources are the CODATA 2022 report on arXiv (2409.03787v1, CC BY 4.0), the BIPM SI Brochure (CC BY 4.0), Swedac's STAFS 2009:26 (a Swedish statute, not protected by copyright under 9 § upphovsrättslagen) and Wikidata (CC0). The two CC BY sources require attribution, which the deck gives (prov:wasDerivedFrom with their titles, creators and licence) together with this report, and a statement of changes: the deck selects 35 of CODATA's constants and the seven defining constants, rounds most values to 5 significant figures, rewrites units in Unicode and adds Swedish names; cards are our own wording. CC BY 4.0 for the deck is compatible with both and with the public-domain and CC0 sources. NIST's CODATA database (NIST Standard Reference Database 121) was not used as a content source although the brief suggested it: NIST says that copyright may be secured in Standard Reference Data, and no page of the database says it is in the public domain, so it was consulted only to verify values (facts, which are not copyrightable); likewise the published Reviews of Modern Physics article (APS, no open licence). Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) were used only to verify that the Swedish names are in use; no text, list or selection was taken from them. Swedish Wikipedia's table "Lista över fysikaliska konstanter" shares 28 of the deck's 35 constants; Selection explains why: both list the best-known CODATA constants, the deck's list follows the brief and CODATA's Table XXXIII and the Swedish-name rule, adds 7 constants the table lacks and leaves out 6 of its rows, and takes none of its order, wording or values. A choice of the standard constants of a field is the obvious one rather than an original selection, so the table is a verification source, not a content source, and the deck is not CC BY-SA. The selection is our own, following the library editor's brief and CODATA's table. All sources are credited in the deck and in this report. Quotations in the evidence (from NE, the APS article, NIST's listing and Swedish Wikipedia) are short verbatim quotations that document the verification, made under the right of quotation (22 § upphovsrättslagen) and, for NE, on the terms NE states for quoting its encyclopedia texts (verbatim, with NE named as the source); they are not part of the deck and are not covered by its CC BY 4.0 licence.

## Method

1. Who did the work. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks (this builder's Wikidata checks and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators); any review rounds by independent AI reviewers are logged under Quality control. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.
2. Which CODATA release. Downloaded NIST's constants home page and version history (Queries) on 2026-10-04. The version history says the 2022 CODATA values are "the latest CODATA values available" (Version 9.0, 9 May 2024), and the home page announces the 2026 adjustment, for which data must be published before 31 December 2026. So the 2022 values (published in Reviews of Modern Physics on 30 April 2025) are the current recommended values on 2026-10-04.
3. Licences. The brief named NIST's CODATA pages as a public-domain content source. NIST's licensing statement says the Secretary of Commerce may secure copyright in Standard Reference Data, and the constants database is NIST Standard Reference Database 121, so it was used for verification only. The CODATA 2022 report itself is on arXiv (2409.03787v1) under CC BY 4.0 and was used as the content source for values, symbols and English names; the BIPM SI Brochure (CC BY 4.0) for the seven defining constants. The published article (APS) carries no open licence and was used only to check that the preprint's table matches it. This makes the deck CC BY 4.0 (see Licensing).
4. Values. Extracted the text of the arXiv PDF with pypdf and read Table XXXIII (PDF pp. 51–55); downloaded NIST's complete ASCII listing (allascii.txt). values.py parses allascii.txt; crosscheck.py found the full digits of 33 of the 35 values in both the arXiv text and the published article's text; the two missing ones, the caesium frequency and the luminous efficacy Kcd, are not in CODATA's tables (a hit for 683 was only part of another number, the neutron-electron mass ratio 1838.683 662 00, so it does not count). The seven defining constants (exact) come from BIPM Table 1 and STAFS 2009:26 bilaga 1.1, which agree with each other and with NIST digit for digit; five of them are also in arXiv Table XXXIII.
5. Rounding convention. Exact values of the seven defining constants are given in full. All other values are rounded to 5 significant figures (round half to even, computed with Python's decimal module from NIST's full digits) and marked with ≈: both the measured constants (whose standard uncertainty is far below the fifth significant figure; the largest relative uncertainty, that of G, is 2.2 × 10⁻⁵) and the constants that are exact since 2019 but have long or endless decimal expansions (ħ, R, F, σ, b, c₁, c₂; CODATA truncates them with "..."; R and F terminate, after 15 and 18 significant digits, the other five never end). Each value card's note says which kind it is. Number format follows the SI Brochure (Section 5.4.4): digits in groups of three separated by a space on both sides of the decimal marker, but no space when there are only four digits; the decimal marker is the point, as in the English SI Brochure and CODATA, since the value is written once for all languages (tag zxx). Powers of ten and unit exponents use Unicode superscripts (× 10⁻³⁴, m s⁻¹); units are written as in CODATA's tables with a space between unit symbols (J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), except that the Planck constant's unit is J s as in the SI Brochure and STAFS (CODATA 2022 writes J Hz⁻¹; the note says so).
6. Symbols. Symbols follow CODATA Table XXXIII and BIPM Table 1, in Unicode: ħ (U+0127), μ (U+03BC), ε (U+03B5), Δ (U+0394), subscript digits (μ₀, ε₀, Z₀, a₀, c₁, c₂) and subscript letters where Unicode has them (mₑ, mₚ, mₙ, mᵤ, rₑ, μₑ). Unicode has no subscript capital letters and no subscript c, d or C, nor a subscript ∞, so ΔνCs, NA, Kcd, λC, μB, μN, lP, mP, tP, TP and R∞ are written with the subscript on the line, and the card's note says which part is the subscript (e.g. "N with subscript A"). The Boltzmann constant's symbol is k, as in CODATA and BIPM Table 1; its note says it is also written kB (as in the SI Brochure's Appendix 1 and Swedish Wikipedia).
7. Selection. Started from the brief (about 35 constants: the seven defining constants plus well-known derived and measured constants) and CODATA Table XXXIII. Kept every constant whose English name is CODATA's and whose Swedish name could be confirmed in at least one Swedish source beyond our own translation (see step 9). One exception: the proton-electron mass ratio, whose Swedish name "kvoten mellan protonens och elektronens massor" is our own descriptive translation (Swedish Wikipedia full-text searches for it and for other phrasings found nothing, and Wikidata Q2912520 has no Swedish label); it was kept because the ratio itself is well attested in Swedish (Swedish Wikipedia, Proton and Elektron: "1836,15 gånger elektronens massa") and the name only describes it. The first and second radiation constants rest on a single Swedish attestation each (see Selection). See Selection for the list and what was left out.
8. English names: CODATA's names from arXiv Table XXXIII and NIST's listing, and BIPM's for the defining constants ("Hyperfine transition frequency of Cs-133" is NIST's name and a Wikidata alias; BIPM says "hyperfine transition frequency of Cs"). Two deliberate departures: "Electron Compton wavelength" (Wikidata's label) instead of CODATA's bare "Compton wavelength", because CODATA also lists Compton wavelengths of other particles; and the luminous efficacy is named in full ("... of monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 10¹² Hz") as in the BIPM text and Wikidata, because "luminous efficacy" alone is a general quantity, not a constant.
9. Swedish names. For the seven defining constants: STAFS 2009:26 bilaga 1.1, Swedish law's definitions of the base units (cesiumfrekvensen, ljusets hastighet i vakuum, Plancks konstant, elementarladdningen, Boltzmanns konstant, Avogadros konstant, ljusutbytet för monokromatisk strålning med frekvensen 540 × 10¹² Hz). For the others: the Swedish Wikidata label where one exists and matches Swedish usage (SPARQL queries under Queries), otherwise our own translation of the CODATA name. Every Swedish name was then checked against Swedish Wikipedia (article titles and leads fetched with the MediaWiki API, full-text search for names without an article, and the table in Fysikalisk konstant) and against Nationalencyklopedin's free article introductions (fetched by headword; ne_fetch.py under Queries). Each card's evidence quotes what those pages say. Names of quantities that are commonly used in the definite form in Swedish are given in the definite form, as NE and Swedish Wikipedia use them (gravitationskonstanten, Bohrradien, Plancklängden).
10. Card text. Front "<name>: symbol" / "<namn>: beteckning" (STAFS's and NE's word for a symbol) and "<name>: value" / "<namn>: värde"; back in no language (zxx): the symbol, or the value with its unit (the fine-structure constant and the proton-electron mass ratio are dimensionless and have none). Notes: on value cards, whether the value is exact or rounded and why (BIPM Table 1 and its statement that the defining constants have no uncertainty; arXiv Table XXXIII's "exact" with "..." for the derived constants; arXiv p. 62: the 2019 SI "made important physicochemical constants such as the molar gas constant R, Faraday constant F, and Stefan-Boltzmann constant σ exactly known"), plus a few facts that help learning, each from a content source: the years since which c, Δν_Cs and Kcd have had fixed values, 1983, 1967 and 1979 (BIPM Appendix 1: Resolution 1 of the 24th CGPM, 2011, PDF pp. 76 and 78, and the abrogation list in Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM, 2018, PDF p. 85), μ₀ before 2019 (BIPM Section 2.3.1), α⁻¹ ≈ 137.04 (arXiv Table XXXIII, inverse fine-structure constant 137.035 999 177), 1 u = m(¹²C)/12 (arXiv Table XXXIII and its footnotes), λₘₐₓ = b/T (arXiv Table XXXIII: "Wien displacement law constants b = λmaxT"), kB as another symbol for k (BIPM Appendix 1), CODATA's unit J Hz⁻¹ for h (arXiv Table XXXIII), ħ read "h-bar" / "h-streck" (Wikidata aliases of Q2115969). On symbol cards, notes only where a subscript cannot be written in Unicode, for ħ, and for k (also written kB).
11. Cross-checks. Every value was checked against NIST's listing (all 35) and, for the 28 non-defining constants, against the published article's Table XXXIII; every defining constant against both BIPM and STAFS. The builder's Wikidata checks confirm, for each constant, the item's NIST/CODATA ID (P1645), its English (and, where Wikidata's wording is the card's, Swedish) label or alias, and its numerical value (P1181) where Wikidata holds the CODATA 2022 or exact value. Where Wikidata disagrees with CODATA 2022 the check was left out and the discrepancy recorded (Quality control, round 0).
12. The dossier was assembled by a script (make_dossier.py, under Queries) from a hand-written file with the metadata and documentation, the card table in the script (names, symbols, units, notes and the Swedish evidence quotes, typed from the pages as fetched) and the downloaded sources: the arXiv, APS and NIST evidence of each card quotes the line of the source's text layer that holds the value's digits, and the Wikidata evidence quotes the labels, IDs and values returned by the SPARQL query q3.
13. Review rounds 1-6 (Quality control) corrected notes (R and F terminate; TP also contains k; c, Δν_Cs and Kcd have had fixed values since 1983, 1967 and 1979, not 2019; the four Planck-unit notes say the value is measured, through G; the Wien note says b gives λₘₐₓ), added notes and evidence (R∞, kB, λₘₐₓ; BIPM evidence for the three years), fixed a Swedish Wikipedia locator, restored NE's pronunciation brackets in two quotes, corrected the attribution of the BIPM evidence to the 24th CGPM (2011) resolution, documented the Selection reasoning (Hartree energy, c₁ and c₂, the overlap with Swedish Wikipedia's table) inlined the helper scripts under Queries and corrected the Faraday constant's digit count in Selection and Method (18 significant digits, not 19). The fixes were applied by editing this dossier directly (round 5 with fix_round5.py, round 6 with fix_round6.py, both under Queries); make_dossier.py was not rerun.

## Selection

35 constants, two cards each: (a) the seven defining constants of the SI (caesium hyperfine frequency, speed of light in vacuum, Planck constant, elementary charge, Boltzmann constant, Avogadro constant, luminous efficacy Kcd); (b) seven constants that have been exact since 2019 as combinations of the defining constants and are written rounded (five of them have endless decimals; R and F terminate, but after 15 and 18 significant digits): reduced Planck constant, molar gas constant, Faraday constant, Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Wien wavelength displacement law constant, first and second radiation constants; (c) 21 measured constants: Newtonian constant of gravitation, vacuum magnetic permeability, vacuum electric permittivity, characteristic impedance of vacuum, fine-structure constant, Rydberg constant, Bohr radius, electron Compton wavelength, classical electron radius, electron, proton and neutron mass, atomic mass constant, proton-electron mass ratio, Bohr magneton, nuclear magneton, electron magnetic moment, and the Planck length, mass, time and temperature. Left out: the Josephson constant, von Klitzing constant, magnetic flux quantum and conductance quantum, because no Swedish source confirming a Swedish name was found (Swedish Wikipedia full-text search for "flödeskvantum", "Josephsonkonstanten" and "von Klitzings konstant" returned no hits, and NE has no article under the names tried); the Hartree energy, for scope: it is the atomic unit of energy (Swedish Wikipedia's article Hartree treats it as "en enhet för energi på atomnivå"), and units are left out (see below). An earlier version of this text gave a missing Swedish name as the reason; that was wrong, since Swedish Wikipedia's table in Fysikalisk konstant names it "Hartree-energi" (a red link). The Swedish names of the first and second radiation constants (c₁, c₂) rest on the same kind of evidence: one row each in that table, red links without an article (MediaWiki API, 2026-10-04), so they are the weakest-attested Swedish names in the deck; they were kept because they are the companions of σ and b in the radiation laws; the standard acceleration of gravity (9.806 65 m s⁻²) and the standard atmosphere (101 325 Pa), which CODATA lists as adopted conventional values, not fundamental constants; the electron volt, the unified atomic mass unit and the Hartree energy as units (the atomic mass constant mᵤ = 1 u is included); the inverse fine-structure constant as a separate card (it is in the α note); the many particle-specific constants (muon, tau, deuteron, helion, magnetic-moment ratios, g-factors) and the proton charge radius, whose value has changed notably between adjustments. The cut-off is the 2022 adjustment: the 2026 CODATA adjustment had not been published on 2026-10-04. Where the list comes from: the brief asked for about 35 well-known constants, the seven SI defining constants first; the rest were chosen from CODATA's Table XXXIII (arXiv, CC BY 4.0), which groups the constants as universal, electromagnetic, atomic and nuclear, and physicochemical: from the universal and physicochemical groups the constants that are exact since 2019, the Planck units and G; from the electromagnetic and atomic groups the constants of the electron, proton and neutron and the magnetons; then filtered by the Swedish-name rule. Overlap with Swedish Wikipedia's table: 28 of the 35 constants are also rows of the 34-row table "Lista över fysikaliska konstanter" in Fysikalisk konstant, because both are lists of the best-known CODATA constants (that table itself cites CODATA 1998). The deck has 7 constants the table lacks (ΔνCs, Kcd, b, λC, rₑ, mₚ/mₑ, TP) and leaves out 6 of its rows (Hartree energy, g-factor of the free electron, proton magnetic moment, proton gyromagnetic ratio, the shielded proton moment ratio and the shielded proton gyromagnetic ratio); its order, grouping, names, symbols and values are not the table's. The table was read only to confirm Swedish names (see Licensing).

## Queries

**Download NIST's complete ASCII listing of the 2022 CODATA values (<scratch> stands for this deck's scratch directory in all commands)** (Fundamental Physical Constants — Complete Listing, 2022 CODATA adjustment (NIST Standard Reference Database 121, allascii.txt))

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/allascii.txt https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Table/allascii.txt
```

**values.py, verbatim: parse allascii.txt and round to 5 significant figures** (Fundamental Physical Constants — Complete Listing, 2022 CODATA adjustment (NIST Standard Reference Database 121, allascii.txt))

```
"""Read the NIST CODATA 2022 ASCII table, pick the deck's constants and round them to 5 significant figures.
Usage: python3 values.py  (prints one line per constant; writes values.json)"""
import json, re
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_EVEN

D = "<scratch>/"
NAMES = [
    "hyperfine transition frequency of Cs-133", "speed of light in vacuum", "Planck constant", "elementary charge",
    "Boltzmann constant", "Avogadro constant", "luminous efficacy", "reduced Planck constant", "molar gas constant",
    "Faraday constant", "Stefan-Boltzmann constant", "Wien wavelength displacement law constant",
    "first radiation constant", "second radiation constant", "Newtonian constant of gravitation",
    "vacuum mag. permeability", "vacuum electric permittivity", "characteristic impedance of vacuum",
    "fine-structure constant", "inverse fine-structure constant", "Rydberg constant", "Bohr radius", "Compton wavelength",
    "classical electron radius", "electron mass", "proton mass", "neutron mass", "atomic mass constant",
    "proton-electron mass ratio", "Bohr magneton", "nuclear magneton", "electron mag. mom.", "Planck length",
    "Planck mass", "Planck time", "Planck temperature",
]
rows = {}
for line in open(D + "allascii.txt", encoding="utf-8"):
    if len(line) < 60 or line.startswith(("-", " ")):
        continue
    name = line[:60].strip()
    rest = line[60:]
    value = rest[:25].strip()
    unc = rest[25:47].strip()
    unit = rest[47:].strip()
    rows[name] = (value, unc, unit)

out = {}
for n in NAMES:
    value, unc, unit = rows[n]
    exact = unc == "(exact)"
    v = value.replace(" ", "").replace("...", "")
    num = Decimal(v.replace("e", "E"))
    q = num.copy_abs()
    exp = q.adjusted()  # power of ten of the leading digit
    rounded = num.scaleb(-exp).quantize(Decimal("1.0000"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
    out[n] = {"value": value, "uncertainty": unc, "unit": unit, "exact": exact,
              "mantissa5": str(rounded), "exp10": exp}
    print(f"{n:45s} | {value:28s} | {unc:24s} | {unit:18s} | 5sf {rounded}e{exp}")
json.dump(out, open(D + "values.json", "w"), indent=1)

```

**crosscheck.py, verbatim: find NIST's digits in the arXiv and APS text layers** (CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787v1, dated 9 September 2024))

```
"""For each constant, find NIST's value digits in the arXiv (CC BY 4.0) and the APS text of the CODATA 2022 paper.
Usage: python3 crosscheck.py"""
import json, re
D = "<scratch>/"
vals = json.load(open(D + "values.json"))
texts = {n: open(D + n + ".txt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
         for n in ("arxiv-2409.03787", "RevModPhys.97.025002")}
def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", s)
ntexts = {k: norm(v) for k, v in texts.items()}
for name, v in vals.items():
    mant = v["value"].split("e")[0].replace("...", "").strip()
    key = norm(mant).lstrip("-")
    res = []
    for k, t in ntexts.items():
        i = t.find(key)
        res.append(f"{k[:6]}:{'found' if i >= 0 else 'MISSING'}")
        if i >= 0 and k.startswith("arxiv"):
            ctx = t[max(0, i - 60):i + len(key) + 40]
    print(f"{name:45s} {key:22s} {' '.join(res)}")

```

**svwiki_titles.py, verbatim** (Swedish Wikipedia: Fysikalisk konstant and the articles on the individual constants)

```
import json, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
# Usage: python3 svwiki_titles.py out.json Title1 Title2 ...
titles = sys.argv[2:]
url = "https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({
    "action": "query", "format": "json", "redirects": "1", "titles": "|".join(titles),
    "prop": "pageprops|extracts", "ppprop": "wikibase_item", "exintro": "1", "explaintext": "1", "exlimit": "max"})
req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"})
data = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60))
open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
q = data["query"]
for r in q.get("redirects", []):
    print("REDIRECT", r["from"], "->", r["to"])
for p in q["pages"].values():
    if "missing" in p:
        print("MISSING", p["title"])
    else:
        print("PAGE", p["title"], p.get("pageprops", {}).get("wikibase_item"), "|", (p.get("extract") or "")[:300].replace("\n", " "))

```

import json, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
# Usage: python3 svwiki_search.py out.json "term1" "term2" ... : Swedish Wikipedia full-text search
res = {}
for term in sys.argv[2:]:
    url = "https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "action": "query", "format": "json", "list": "search", "srsearch": term, "srlimit": "8"})
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"})
    data = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60))
    res[term] = data
    print("=== " + term + " (" + str(data["query"]["searchinfo"]["totalhits"]) + " hits)")
    for h in data["query"]["search"]:
        snip = h["snippet"].replace('<span class="searchmatch">', "[").replace("</span>", "]")
        print("  " + h["title"] + " | " + snip)
open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))

import sys, glob, re, os
# Usage: python3 kwic.py <glob> term1 term2 ... : prints each occurrence with context
files = sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1]))
for term in sys.argv[2:]:
    print("=== " + term)
    for f in files:
        t = open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(term), t, re.I):
            s = t[max(0, m.start() - 110):m.end() + 110].replace("\n", " ")
            print("  [" + os.path.basename(f) + "] " + s)

**ne_fetch.py, verbatim** (Nationalencyklopedin (NE), uppslagsverket: free introductions of the articles on the constants)

```
import sys, os, urllib.parse, urllib.request, re, html
# Usage: python3 ne_fetch.py outdir slug1 slug2 ... : fetches NE encyclopedia pages (lång) and prints the
# free introductory text (verification only; nothing is copied into the deck).
out = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
for slug in sys.argv[2:]:
    url = "https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/" + urllib.parse.quote("lång") + "/" + urllib.parse.quote(slug)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"})
    try:
        page = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except Exception as e:
        print("FAIL", slug, e)
        continue
    open(os.path.join(out, slug + ".html"), "w").write(page)
    text = re.sub(r"<(script|style|noscript)[^>]*>.*?</\1>", " ", page, flags=re.S)
    text = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", text))
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
    i = text.find("Skriv ut")
    j = text.find("Information om artikeln")
    print("OK", slug, "|", text[i + 9:j].strip()[:600] if i >= 0 else text[:300])

**QC rounds 1-3: the script that applied the fixes to this dossier, including the exact-fraction check that R = NA k and F = NA e terminate and c₂ = hc/k does not** (CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787v1, dated 9 September 2024))

```
"""Apply the fixes from QC rounds 1-3 to authored/physical-constants.json."""
import json, re, urllib.parse
from fractions import Fraction

P = "/home/antwika/dev/github/antwika/solid-memo/.claude/worktrees/authored-decks/packages/deck-library/authored/physical-constants.json"
S = "<scratch>/"
d = json.load(open(P, encoding="utf-8"))
cards = {c["id"]: c for c in d["cards"]}
changed = set()
T = "2026-10-04"

# --- exact arithmetic for R and F (QC round 1) ---
NA = Fraction("6.02214076e23"); k = Fraction("1.380649e-23"); e = Fraction("1.602176634e-19")
h = Fraction("6.62607015e-34"); c = Fraction(299792458)
def terminates(f):
    q = f.denominator
    for p in (2, 5):
        while q % p == 0:
            q //= p
    return q == 1
R = NA * k; F = NA * e; c2 = h * c / k
print("R", float(R), terminates(R), "F", float(F), terminates(F), "c2 terminates", terminates(c2))
assert terminates(R) and terminates(F) and not terminates(c2)
assert R == Fraction("8.31446261815324") and F == Fraction("96485.3321233100184")

def note(cid, en, sv):
    cards[cid]["backNote"] = {"en": en, "sv": sv}
    changed.add(cid)

note("molar-gas-constant-value",
     "Exact since 2019, as the product of the Avogadro and Boltzmann constants (8.314 462 618 153 24 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹); rounded to 5 significant figures.",
     "Exakt sedan 2019, som produkten av Avogadros och Boltzmanns konstanter (8,314 462 618 153 24 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹); avrundat till 5 värdesiffror.")

     "Exact since 2019, as the product of the Avogadro constant and the elementary charge (96 485.332 123 310 018 4 C mol⁻¹); rounded to 5 significant figures.",
     "Exakt sedan 2019, som produkten av Avogadros konstant och elementarladdningen (96 485,332 123 310 018 4 C mol⁻¹); avrundat till 5 värdesiffror.")
for cid, name in (("molar-gas-constant-value", "R = NA k"), ("faraday-constant-value", "F = NA e")):
    cards[cid]["evidence"].append({

        "locator": "Section 2.2, Table 1. The seven defining constants of the SI (PDF p. 14); the full value computed from it",
        "says": ("NA 6.022 140 76 × 1023 mol−1 and k 1.380 649 × 10−23 J K−1 [their exact product, computed with Python's fractions module: 8.314 462 618 153 24, a terminating decimal]"
                 if cid.startswith("molar") else
                 "NA 6.022 140 76 × 1023 mol−1 and e 1.602 176 634 × 10−19 C [their exact product, computed with Python's fractions module: 96 485.332 123 310 018 4, a terminating decimal]"),
        "retrieved": T})

note("planck-temperature-value",
     "Planck unit, built from G, ħ, c and k. CODATA 2022 value, rounded to 5 significant figures.",
     "Planckenhet, bildad av G, ħ, c och k. Värde enligt CODATA 2022, avrundat till 5 värdesiffror.")

# Boltzmann: also written kB
note("boltzmann-constant-symbol", "Also written kB (k with subscript B).", "Skrivs även kB (k med nedsänkt B).")
cards["boltzmann-constant-symbol"]["evidence"] += [

     "retrieved": T},

     "says": "\"[[Boltzmanns konstant]] | <math>k_B,\\ k</math> | 1,380 649 · 10<sup>−23</sup> J·K<sup>−1</sup> (definierad)\"",
     "retrieved": T}]

# Rydberg: subscript note
note("rydberg-constant-symbol", "R with subscript ∞.", "R med nedsänkt ∞.")
cards["rydberg-constant-symbol"]["evidence"].append({

    "says": "\"[[Rydbergs konstant]] | <math>R_\\infty\\,</math>\" [R with subscript ∞]",

            "Bohrmagneton": ["bohrmagneton"]}
def ne_url(slug):
    return "https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/" + urllib.parse.quote("lång") + "/" + urllib.parse.quote(slug)
for card in d["cards"]:

"""Apply the fixes from QC round 5 to authored/physical-constants.json."""
import json

P = "/home/antwika/dev/github/antwika/solid-memo/.claude/worktrees/authored-decks/packages/deck-library/authored/physical-constants.json"
d = json.load(open(P, encoding="utf-8"))
cards = {c["id"]: c for c in d["cards"]}

# 1. BIPM resolution attribution
OLD76 = "Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM (2018), considering (PDF p. 76)"
OLD78 = "Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM (2018), decides (PDF p. 78)"
NEW76 = "Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 24th CGPM (2011), considering (PDF p. 76)"
NEW78 = "Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 24th CGPM (2011), 'In consequence, on the date chosen for the implementation of the revision of the SI' (PDF p. 78)"
LOC85 = "Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM (2018), Appendix 1 'Abrogation of former definitions of the base units' (PDF p. 85)"
says85 = {
    "speed-of-light-value": "the definition of the metre in force since 1983 (17th meeting of the CGPM, Resolution 1), is abrogated,",
    "caesium-frequency-value": "the definition of the second in force since 1967/68 (13th meeting of the CGPM, Resolution 1) is abrogated,",
    "luminous-efficacy-value": "the definition of the candela in force since 1979 (16th meeting of the CGPM, Resolution 3) is abrogated,",
}
n = 0
for cid, s in says85.items():
    ev = cards[cid]["evidence"]
    for e in ev:
        if e.get("locator") == OLD76:
            e["locator"] = NEW76; n += 1
        elif e.get("locator") == OLD78:
            e["locator"] = NEW78; n += 1
    ev.append({"source": "bipm-si-brochure", "locator": LOC85, "says": s, "retrieved": "2026-10-04"})
assert n == 4, n

m = d["method"]
for i, step in enumerate(m):
    if "Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM, PDF pp. 76 and 78" in step:
        m[i] = step.replace(
            "(BIPM Appendix 1, Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM, PDF pp. 76 and 78)",
            "(BIPM Appendix 1: Resolution 1 of the 24th CGPM, 2011, PDF pp. 76 and 78, and the abrogation list in Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM, 2018, PDF p. 85)")
        m[i] = m[i].replace("the symbol, or the value with unit.", "the symbol, or the value with its unit (the fine-structure constant and the proton-electron mass ratio are dimensionless and have none).")
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("method step not found")

# 2. Planck unit capitalisation
for cid in ("planck-length-value", "planck-mass-value", "planck-time-value", "planck-temperature-value"):
    note = cards[cid]["backNote"]
    assert "planck unit" in note["en"] and "planckenhet" in note["sv"]
    note["en"] = note["en"].replace(": planck unit,", ": a Planck unit,")
    note["sv"] = note["sv"].replace(": planckenhet,", ": en Planckenhet,")

# 3. Method's last step
assert m[-1].startswith("Review rounds 1-3")
m[-1] = ("Review rounds 1-5 (Quality control) corrected notes (R and F terminate; TP also contains k; c, Δν_Cs and Kcd have had fixed values since 1983, 1967 and 1979, not 2019; "
         "the four Planck-unit notes say the value is measured, through G; the Wien note says b gives λₘₐₓ), added notes and evidence (R∞, kB, λₘₐₓ; BIPM evidence for the three years), "
         "fixed a Swedish Wikipedia locator, restored NE's pronunciation brackets in two quotes, corrected the attribution of the BIPM evidence to the 24th CGPM (2011) resolution, "
         "documented the Selection reasoning (Hartree energy, c₁ and c₂, the overlap with Swedish Wikipedia's table) and inlined the helper scripts under Queries. "
         "The fixes were applied by editing this dossier directly (round 5 with fix_round5.py, under Queries); make_dossier.py was not rerun.")

# 4. Description
de = d["description"]
assert "one for its value with unit." in de["en"] and "ett efter dess värde med enhet." in de["sv"]
de["en"] = de["en"].replace("one for its value with unit.", "one for its value (with unit where it has one).")
de["sv"] = de["sv"].replace("ett efter dess värde med enhet.", "ett efter dess värde (med enhet där den har en).")

# 5. Queries
SCRIPT = open(__file__, encoding="utf-8").read().replace(
    "<scratch>/", "<scratch>/")
d["queries"].append({
    "source": "bipm-si-brochure",
    "purpose": "QC round 5: read the resolution headings and texts on PDF pp. 76-78 and 84-86 of the downloaded SI Brochure",
    "query": "uv run --with pypdf python3 -c \"\nfrom pypdf import PdfReader\nr=PdfReader('<scratch>/bipm-si-brochure-9-en.pdf')\nfor p in (75,76,77,83,84,85):\n  t=r.pages[p].extract_text()\n  print('=== PDF p',p+1); print(t[:1800])\n\"",
})
d["queries"].append({
    "source": "bipm-si-brochure",
    "purpose": "QC round 5: the script that applied the fixes to this dossier, verbatim (the QC round entry it appends is elided here)",
    "query": SCRIPT.split("# 6. QC round")[0],
})

# 6. QC round

## Quality control

7 rounds, 50 findings: 32 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 17 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (102 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Source agreement and machine checks: every value against arXiv/CODATA 2022, NIST and (defining constants) BIPM and STAFS; every Swedish name against Swedish Wikipedia and NE; the builder's Wikidata checks. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 70 cards; the licences of all sources.

102 Wikidata checks pass (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py check physical-constants, 2026-10-04): the NIST/CODATA ID (P1645) of all 35 items; the English label or alias of 33 (all but the vacuum magnetic permeability and the proton-electron mass ratio, whose CODATA names Wikidata lacks); the Swedish label or alias of 12 where Wikidata's wording is the card's (Plancks konstant, Boltzmanns konstant, Diracs konstant, h-streck, allmänna gaskonstanten, Faradays konstant, Stefan–Boltzmanns konstant, gravitationskonstanten, magnetiska konstanten, elektriska konstanten, finstrukturkonstanten, Bohrmagnetonen); and the numerical value (P1181) of 22 constants where Wikidata holds the exact or CODATA 2022 value. All 35 values agree digit for digit between NIST's listing and the content sources (arXiv Table XXXIII for 33 values (all but the caesium frequency and Kcd), BIPM Table 1 and STAFS for the seven defining constants), and the 28 non-defining values also with the published article. Discrepancies and decisions are listed as findings; no Wikidata check was dropped to make the build pass other than those listed.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 70 cards: every value against NIST's live CODATA 2022 listing (re-rounded independently), every symbol, the notes, Selection and Method.

All 35 values and 35 symbols were confirmed. Three errors in notes: the R and F notes claimed endless decimals, but NA·k and NA·e are products of terminating decimals and terminate (8.314 462 618 153 24 and 96 485.332 123 310 018 4, the values the deck's own Wikidata checks expect); the same claim was in Selection and Method; and the Planck temperature note omitted k. Two suggestions: plain-letter subscripts (mP vs mₚ, NA) and the alternative symbol kB. Verified each finding with exact fractions and the sources; fixed the errors and accepted the kB note.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| molar-gas-constant-value | The note says R is exact but its decimals never end; R = NA·k = 8.314 462 618 153 24 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ exactly, a terminating decimal. | Confirmed with Python fractions (qc1_patch.py). Note now: 'Exact since 2019, as the product of the Avogadro and Boltzmann constants (8.314 462 618 153 24 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹); rounded to 5 significant figures.' (sv likewise, with decimal comma). Added BIPM Table 1 evidence for the computed product. | fixed |
| faraday-constant-value | The note says F's decimals never end; F = NA·e = 96 485.332 123 310 018 4 C mol⁻¹ exactly, a terminating decimal. | Confirmed with Python fractions. Note now gives the full exact value and says it is rounded to 5 significant figures (sv likewise). Added BIPM Table 1 evidence for the computed product. | fixed |
| planck-temperature-value | The note says the Planck temperature is built from G, ħ and c; TP = (ħc⁵/G)^½/k also contains k. | Confirmed by the card's own arXiv evidence "(¯hc5/G)1/2/k". Note now: 'Planck unit, built from G, ħ, c and k. ...' / 'Planckenhet, bildad av G, ħ, c och k. ...'. | fixed |
| deck | Selection (b) and Method step 5 say all seven exact-derived constants have endless decimals; R and F terminate. | Confirmed (ħ, σ, c₁ contain π, b the Wien root, c₂ = hc/k does not terminate since 1 380 649 has prime factors other than 2 and 5). Selection (b) now says 'exact since 2019 as combinations of the defining constants and are written rounded (five of them have endless decimals; R and F terminate ...)'; the Rounding step says 'long or endless decimal expansions (CODATA truncates them with "...")'. The other five value notes ('decimals never end') are correct and unchanged. | fixed |
| planck-mass-symbol | Suggestion: plain-letter subscripts (mP, NA) look like mₚ or 'N/A'; optionally add 'often also written N_A' to the Avogadro note. | Declined: Unicode has no subscript capitals, every such card already has a note naming the subscript, and the Planck mass note explicitly contrasts mP with mₚ. Adding TeX-style N_A would introduce a third notation. | rejected |
| boltzmann-constant-symbol | Suggestion: much teaching material writes kB; add 'Also written k_B'. | Accepted. Note: 'Also written kB (k with subscript B).' / 'Skrivs även kB (k med nedsänkt B).' Evidence added: SI Brochure Appendix 1, 23rd CGPM Resolution 12 ("the Boltzmann constant kB") and Swedish Wikipedia's table ("k_B, k"). The back stays k (CODATA, BIPM Table 1). | fixed |
